raw_response:
I am 69 years old, and I have farmed these 3.5 mu in Quzhou for 45 years. I never went to school, but I know this land better than any book. My wife and I work it together, and our son sends money back from his job in the city, so we are not desperate. We have our well, which is our lifeline.

It is late April. My winter wheat went in last October after I ploughed the field and spread the base fertilizer. I used the improved Jinmai seeds from the township shop — they are reliable, and I have used them for many years. I already irrigated once at green-up in March. Now the wheat is jointing, so I will irrigate again in the next few days and top-dress with urea. I will give it one more water when the grain is filling in May. I do not water more than that — electricity for the pump costs money, and too much water makes the wheat lodge. I will spray for aphids and rust twice if I see them, but not more. I put down compound fertilizer before planting, and I will add more nitrogen at jointing. I expect about 420 kg per mu from the wheat if the weather holds.

After I harvest the wheat in early June, I must move fast. I will run the rotary tiller to prepare the ground and plant hybrid maize — probably Zhengdan or a similar yellow corn that the seed dealer recommends. It grows fast in the summer heat. I will put down fertilizer at planting, and then side-dress once when the plants are knee-high. I will irrigate twice: once right after planting if the soil is dry, and again at the big trumpet stage in July if the rains do not come. I will spray for armyworm and borers twice. I am hoping for 450 kg per mu from the maize. That gives us enough grain for our own use and some cash from selling the rest.

I farm the way my father taught me, with small adjustments from what I see works on my neighbors' fields. I do not waste money on fancy inputs, but I do not starve the crops either. At my age, I take it steady.
